title: On the Central Maximal Function in $\mathbb{R}^n$
summary: We consider the central Hardy--Littlewood maximal operator in $\mathbb{R}^n$. For every integer $n\geq1$, we construct two bounded, nonnegative functions $f,g\in L^1(\mathbb{R}^n)$ that differ on a set of positive measure and satisfy $M_cf(x)=M_cg(x)$ at every point $x\in\mathbb{R}^n$. Thus the central maximal operator is not injective on the nonnegative cone of $L^1(\mathbb{R}^n)$. The functions can have compact support; when $n\geq2$, they can also be chosen radial, either with compact support or strictly positive throughout the space.
